name: AWS EC2 P5en (NVIDIA H200 SXM, on-demand + Capacity Blocks)
price_basis: per H200 SXM GPU-hour; 8x H200 per p5en.48xlarge. On-demand us-east-1 $63.296/instance-hr / 8 = $7.912 (identical in us-west-2). Capacity Block $54.92/8 = $6.865 in us-east (n. Virginia, Ohio, Atlanta local zone, N. California, Oregon) and $49.928/8 = $6.241 in eu-stockholm, eu-london, eu-spain and the ap regions. Fetched 2026-10-03.
notes: The most expensive credible H200 hour among the hyperscalers in this slice, and scheduled to get worse: AWS's published forward schedule for 2026-10-07 raises the P5en Capacity Block rate from $6.865 to $7.895 and P5e from $5.970 to $6.866. Carries the same $0.00 'no capacity' sentinel as p5 in the price list, so on-demand p5en is likewise not reliably purchasable. p5en differs from p5e by using Nitro v5 and 3rd-gen EFA, giving roughly 35% lower network latency than P5 and Gen5 PCIe CPU-GPU bandwidth (100 Gbps EBS vs 80). That is the reason to pay the ~$1.05/GPU-hr premium over the p5e Capacity Block rate - and the reason to skip p5en entirely if you are not doing distributed training. No 1-year or 3-year savings plan is published for p5en; the dynamic Capacity Block is the only discount channel.
